139	## Installing into agent harnesses
140	
141	Astrid ships its own skills layer for the three supported agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes). One command installs the `_core` skill plus any per-pack skills into every harness it detects on the machine:
142	
143	```bash
144	python3 -m astrid skills list                 # show installable packs and current per-harness state
145	python3 -m astrid skills install --all        # install every pack into every detected harness
146	python3 -m astrid skills doctor               # verify symlinks resolve and AGENTS.md block parses
147	python3 -m astrid skills uninstall _core      # remove from all harnesses
148	```
149	
150	Default mechanism is per-pack symlinks under `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.codex/skills/`, and `${HERMES_HOME:-~/.hermes}/skills/`. Codex additionally maintains an idempotent fenced block in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` listing each installed pack. Hermes accepts an opt-in `--mechanism external-dir` that registers the whole `astrid/packs` tree via `~/.hermes/config.yaml` `skills.external_dirs` instead of per-pack symlinks.
151	
152	If no harness is installed, Astrid prints a one-line nudge to stderr at most once every seven days when you run a non-`skills` subcommand. Suppress with `ARTAGENTS_NO_NUDGE=1` or `--quiet`.
153	
154	See `docs/skills-install.md` for the SkillDescriptor contract and the `metadata.hermes.*` extension block.
155	
156	## Make something new
157	
158	Read `docs/creating-tools.md`, then follow this build order — every step before falling back to the next:
159	
160	1. **Compose existing executors first.** `python3 -m astrid executors list` and `inspect` the candidates. If existing executors can be wired together to do the job, build only an orchestrator that calls them.
161	2. **Create the missing executors next.** Each new executor must do *one* concrete, focused unit of work — independently runnable, inspectable, and testable. Don't pack workflow logic into an executor; that belongs in an orchestrator.
162	3. **Then write the orchestrator.** It composes the executors (existing + newly created) into the workflow. Orchestrators may call other orchestrators; executors must not.
163	
164	Skipping step 1 to write a god-orchestrator that bakes in network calls and business logic is the anti-pattern. Suspect it whenever a `run.py` grows past a couple of hundred lines without delegating to executors.
165	
166	Templates:
167	
168	- `docs/templates/executor/` — one concrete unit of work
169	- `docs/templates/orchestrator/` — a workflow that combines executors
170	- `docs/templates/element/` — a reusable render building block
171	
172	Content lives under packs at `astrid/packs/<pack>/`. Executor folders use the layout `astrid/packs/<pack>/<slug>/{executor.yaml,STAGE.md,run.py}` and orchestrator folders use `astrid/packs/<pack>/<slug>/{orchestrator.yaml,STAGE.md,run.py}`, with optional local `src/` modules. Element folders live at `astrid/packs/<pack>/elements/<kind>/<id>/{component.tsx,element.yaml}` (kind ∈ {effects, animations, transitions}). Top-level `astrid/*.py` files are shared libraries or system commands, not alternate runnable implementations. Executor and orchestrator ids are always qualified — `<pack>.<name>` (e.g. `builtin.cut`, `external.vibecomfy.run`); bare ids are rejected.
173	
174	Do not chain pipeline internals by hand unless you are debugging one specific stage. If the user gives a topic instead of a brief, use a brief-generation executor coordinated by an orchestrator — don't fake source media just to enter a source-video path. Render requires the `hype.timeline.json` and `hype.assets.json` pair produced by cut; don't skip cut unless both files already exist.
175	
176	## Defaults
177	
178	Built-in orchestrators: `builtin.hype`, `builtin.event_talks`, `builtin.thumbnail_maker`.
179	
180	Built-in executors include `builtin.transcribe`, `builtin.cut`, `builtin.render`, `builtin.validate`, `builtin.understand` (audio/visual/video dispatcher; pass `--mode {audio,visual,video}`), `builtin.generate_image` (with a `saint-peter-of-banodoco` preset for the onboarding portrait), and the rest of the pipeline. External executors include `external.moirae` and `external.vibecomfy.run` (executor only, not an orchestrator).
181	
182	Element source priority: active theme → `astrid/packs/local/elements/<kind>/<id>` (gitignored scratch pack) → `astrid/packs/builtin/elements/<kind>/<id>`. Forking copies the source element into `astrid/packs/local/`, auto-creating `astrid/packs/local/pack.yaml` and rewriting the element's `pack_id` to `local`.
183	
184	```bash
185	python3 -m astrid elements fork effects text-card
186	```
187	
188	## Rules
189	
190	- Generated files live under `runs/` (or another ignored output directory) and stay out of git. Don't commit source media, rendered videos, local dependency envs, or secrets.
191	- Don't print or hardcode API keys; use `--env-file` or nearby `.env` files.
192	- Treat curated tool stages as protected unless explicitly asked to edit them — notably `astrid/packs/external/moirae/STAGE.md` and `astrid/packs/external/vibecomfy/STAGE.md`.
193	- Orchestrators may call declared child orchestrators; executors must not call orchestrators.
194	
195	After adding or renaming effects, animations, transitions, or theme elements:
196	
197	```bash
198	python3 scripts/gen_effect_registry.py
199	cd remotion && npm run gen-types
200	```
201	
202	After editing `short_description` / `keywords` on any executor, orchestrator, or element manifest, refresh the capability index in this file:
203	
204	```bash
205	python3 scripts/gen_capability_index.py
206	```
207	
208	## Adding overlays to a rendered video
209	
210	Quick recipe: take any `.mp4` and overlay text captions / a wordmark via the timeline + Remotion path.
211	
212	### The two-file model
213	
214	- `timeline.json` — defines tracks and clips. Schema: `@banodoco/timeline-schema` (see `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts`). Top level: `{theme, theme_overrides?, tracks, clips}`. Each clip has `id, at (seconds), track, clipType, asset?, hold? | from/to, text?, params?, effects?, x?/y?/width?/height?`.
215	- `assets.json` — `{"assets": {"<id>": {file?: <relative-or-absolute-path>, type?, resolution?, fps?, duration?}}}`. Files must share a common parent so the renderer's local HTTP server can serve them.
216	
217	### Layering rule (gotcha)
218	
219	Visual tracks render in **reversed** array order (`TimelineComposition.tsx`: `[...getVisualTracks(timeline)].reverse()`). To put overlays on top, list the overlay track **first** in `timeline.tracks`.
220	
221	### Timeline design conventions
222	
223	Use one track per editing concern, not one catch-all overlay track. A maintainable visual stack usually reads top-to-bottom as `brand` or persistent CTA, `captions`, moment-specific `fx` or text callouts, `broll`, then `source`; audio tracks follow visual tracks. Because visual tracks render in reversed order, the first visual track in `tracks` is the top layer. Keep clip ids prefixed by concern (`brand_`, `cap_`, `fx_`, `broll_`, `src_`, `audio_`) so later patches can target the right layer without re-reading every clip. Split a track as soon as clips have different lifetimes, ownership, or review criteria; for example, do not mix persistent branding, subtitles, and transient emphasis cards on one track.
224	
225	The canonical small fixture is `examples/hype.timeline.json`. Read it before hand-authoring a timeline; `examples/hype.timeline.full.json` is for schema coverage, not design guidance.
226	
227	### Minimal maintainable example: video + caption + wordmark
228	
229	```jsonc
230	// assets.json
231	{
232	  "assets": {
233	    "src": {"file": "video.mp4", "type": "video/mp4", "resolution": "1920x1080", "fps": 30, "duration": 49.5}
234	  }
235	}
236	```
237	
238	```jsonc
239	// timeline.json
240	{
241	  "theme": "banodoco-default",
242	  "theme_overrides": {"visual": {"canvas": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": 30}}},
243	  "tracks": [
244	    {"id": "brand", "kind": "visual", "label": "Brand"},
245	    {"id": "captions", "kind": "visual", "label": "Captions"},
246	    {"id": "source", "kind": "visual", "label": "Source"}
247	  ],
248	  "clips": [
249	    {"id": "src_main", "at": 0, "track": "source", "clipType": "media", "asset": "src", "from": 0, "to": 49.5},
250	    {
251	      "id": "brand_wordmark", "at": 0, "track": "brand", "clipType": "text", "hold": 49.5,
252	      "text": {"content": "REIGH", "fontSize": 24, "color": "#ffffff", "align": "right"},
253	      "params": {"anchor": "top-right", "offsetX": 64, "offsetY": 48, "weight": 700,
254	                 "textShadow": "0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.75)"}
255	    },
256	    {
257	      "id": "cap_search", "at": 3, "track": "captions", "clipType": "text", "hold": 10,
258	      "effects": {"fade_in": 0.4, "fade_out": 0.4},
259	      "text": {"content": "search 1.2 million messages", "fontSize": 38, "color": "#ffffff", "align": "right"},
260	      "params": {"anchor": "bottom-right", "offsetX": 80, "offsetY": 140, "maxWidth": 720, "weight": 600,
261	                 "textShadow": "0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.85)"}
262	    }
263	  ]
264	}
265	```
266	
267	### Adding music or another audio track
268	
269	Audio is a first-class track kind — there is no separate audio pipeline and no post-render ffmpeg mux. Declare an `audio` track, register the file as an asset, and add a `media` clip on the audio track. Remotion bakes audio into the rendered MP4 directly.
270	
271	```jsonc
272	// assets.json — add a music asset alongside your video
273	{
274	  "assets": {
275	    "src":   {"file": "video.mp4", "type": "video/mp4", "duration": 47.6},
276	    "music": {"file": "music.mp3", "type": "audio/mpeg"}
277	  }
278	}
279	```
280	
281	```jsonc
282	// timeline.json — add an audio track and a media clip on it
283	"tracks": [
284	  {"id": "source", "kind": "visual", "label": "Source"},
285	  {"id": "a1",     "kind": "audio",  "label": "Music"}
286	],
287	"clips": [
288	  {"id": "src_main", "at": 0, "track": "source", "clipType": "media", "asset": "src", "from": 0, "to": 47.6},
289	  {
290	    "id": "audio_music",
291	    "at": 0,                 // timeline time the clip starts playing
292	    "track": "a1",
293	    "clipType": "media",     // audio uses the same `media` clipType as video
294	    "asset": "music",
295	    "from": 5,               // trim: start the source 5s in
296	    "to": 52.6,              // trim end in source time (clip plays for to-from = 47.6s)
297	    "volume": 1.0,           // 0..1 scalar, multiplies track volume
298	    "params": {"fadeIn": 0, "fadeOut": 2.5}
299	  }
300	]
301	```
302	
303	Field semantics (the parts that aren't obvious from `types.ts`):
304	
305	- `from` / `to` are in **source-media time, seconds** — they trim the asset, they don't move the clip on the timeline. The clip's timeline duration is `to - from`. To start the music *later* in the video, raise `clip.at`, not `from`.
306	- `volume` is a scalar 0..1; track and clip volume multiply. `track.muted: true` forces silence regardless.
307	- `params.fadeIn` / `params.fadeOut` are in seconds, taper at the clip's local start/end. Implemented inside `AudioTrack.tsx` as a per-frame volume function — no afade pre-bake needed.
308	- Local audio paths in `assets.json` resolve like local video: the render runner picks a common parent of all asset files and serves them over `http://localhost:<port>/...`. Remotion's `<Audio src>` consumes that URL natively.
309	
310	You should not need ffmpeg's `atrim` / `afade` / `amix` for any normal "music under the video" use case. Reach for ffmpeg only for things Remotion genuinely doesn't model (offline loudness normalization, sample-accurate cross-fades between two music beds, etc.).
311	
312	### Rendering
313	
314	```bash
315	PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 \
316	ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC=$(pwd)/remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/typescript/src \
317	python3 -m astrid.packs.builtin.render.run \
318	  --timeline runs/<my-run>/timeline.json \
319	  --assets runs/<my-run>/assets.json \
320	  --out runs/<my-run>/composed.mp4
321	```
322	
323	The `ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC` env var points the codegen at `node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition` — without it, `gen_effect_registry.py` writes to `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/packages/timeline-composition` instead of the place Remotion actually imports from. Until that's fixed upstream, set the env var on every render whenever your effect/animation set changes.
324	
325	### Where the schemas live (authoritative)
326	
327	- Timeline + clip Zod schemas: `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts`
328	- Composition (clip → component dispatch, layering): `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/typescript/src/TimelineComposition.tsx`
329	- Effect / animation registries: generated by `scripts/gen_effect_registry.py` into `effects.generated.ts` etc. inside the `@banodoco/timeline-composition` package
330	- Python timeline IO + validation: `astrid/timeline.py`
331	- Render entrypoint: `astrid/packs/builtin/render/run.py`
332	
333	### Available elements
334	
335	Run `python3 -m astrid elements list` (or `inspect <kind> <id> --json` for a single element). At time of writing:
336	
337	- effects: `text-card` (text rendering — see note below)
338	- animations: `fade`, `fade-up`, `scale-in`, `slide-left`, `slide-up`, `type-on`
339	- transitions: `cross-fade`, `fade`
340	
341	### Text rendering note (important)
342	
343	The built-in `text-card` component is `() => null` — it expects a theme override to do the real DOM rendering. If your theme doesn't ship one, fork into the local pack:
344	
345	```bash
346	python3 -m astrid elements fork effects text-card
347	# edit astrid/packs/local/elements/effects/text-card/component.tsx
348	python3 scripts/gen_effect_registry.py     # regenerates registry
349	```
350	
351	The local-pack TextCard in this repo already supports anchored positioning (`params.anchor` ∈ {top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right}, plus `offsetX/offsetY/maxWidth/background/padding/borderRadius/lineHeight/weight/letterSpacing/textShadow`) and reads `clip.effects.{fade_in,fade_out}` (seconds) for entry/exit fades.
352	
353	### 5-minute "add a caption" recipe
354	
355	1. Drop your source `.mp4` into `runs/<name>/`.
356	2. Copy the JSON snippets above into `runs/<name>/{timeline,assets}.json`. Adjust `at`, `hold`, `text.content`, and `params.anchor`; add a new track when the new clip is a new concern, not just another caption.
357	3. Render with the command above.
358	4. ffprobe / open the `composed.mp4`.
359	5. If captions don't appear after editing the local-pack component, blow away `remotion/node_modules/.cache` — Remotion's webpack caches aggressively across renders.

7	
8	# Orchestrator V1 Plan
9	
10	## 1. Executive Summary
11	
12	Astrid V1 adds task mode: a single-host, file-based way to put an agent inside a frozen plan and advance it through creative pipeline work one permitted command at a time. The plan can mix code, AI, and human steps without introducing a daemon, web server, or pretend sandbox. Runtime behavior collapses to three step kinds: `code` for deterministic argv subprocesses, `attested` for agent or human work that requires identity-pinned acknowledgment and evidence, and `nested` for child-plan delegation whose structure remains visible to the gate for hashing and pinning. Iteration and fan-out are not separate kinds; they are body attributes that can wrap any step or nested block through `repeat.until` and `repeat.for_each`. Migration stays additive: existing pack mechanics, JSON manifests, and `python` / `command` runtime kinds keep working while the new Python DSL compiles hash-pinned task plans for V1 runs.
13	
14	## 2. Goals & Non-Goals
15	
16	Goals: freeze task-mode runs around immutable `plan.json`; gate every command before runner side effects; use exactly `code`, `attested`, and `nested`; model loops through `repeat`; use golden `events.jsonl` as regression output; split lifecycle verbs by audience; keep packs and legacy orchestrator manifests loadable.
17	
18	Non-goals: no daemon, no web server, no HMAC or keyed crypto, no `.index.db`, no shared CAS, and no sandbox against malicious agents. V1 is honor-based with strong logging and accidental-edit tripwires.
19	
20	## 3. Data Model
21	
22	Task-mode state lives under `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/astrid-projects/<slug>/`:
23	
24	```text
25	active_run.json
26	runs/<run-id>/plan.json
27	runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl
28	runs/<run-id>/AGENT.md
29	runs/<run-id>/steps/<step-id>/produces/
30	runs/<run-id>/steps/<step-id>/iterations/NNN/
31	runs/<run-id>/steps/<step-id>/items/<item-id>/
32	runs/<run-id>/inbox/
33	.cas/<sha256>
34	```
35	
36	`active_run.json` is `{ "run_id": "<run-id>", "plan_hash": "sha256:<hex>" }`. `plan.json` is immutable after `astrid start`, supersedes checklist naming because the shape is a tree, and is the runtime truth the gate hashes; existing `OrchestratorPlan` / `OrchestratorPlanStep` in `astrid/core/orchestrator/runner.py` remain dry-run display scaffolding. `events.jsonl` is append-only and hash-chained as plain `sha256(prev_hash + canonical_event_json)` with no HMAC. There is no `.index.db`; status and audit read files directly.
37	
38	## 4. Step Kinds
39	
40	`code` is deterministic argv subprocess execution. It is a strict superset of `RUNTIME_KINDS={python,command}` in `astrid/core/orchestrator/schema.py`, may call `python3 -m astrid executors run <name> ...`, and must not call `astrid orchestrators run`.
41	
42	`attested` is agent or human work with instructions, produces, identity-pinned ack, and evidence. Agent attestations require `--agent <id>`. Human attestations require `--actor <name>` matching `ARTAGENTS_ACTOR`. Self-acks and unpinned actors are rejected.
43	
44	`nested` is the only sub-orchestrator delegation mechanism. The child plan is data in the compiled tree so the gate can hash, pin, and derive cursors from its structure.
45	
46	## 5. Iteration & Fan-Out
47	
48	Iteration and fan-out are body attributes, not kinds. `repeat.until` supports `user_approves`, `verifier_passes`, and `quorum`, with `max_iterations` and `on_exhaust`; attempts write under `iterations/NNN/`. `repeat.for_each` expands a body over an input set and writes per-item state under `items/<item-id>/`; `ack --item <id>` supports partial approval.
49	
50	## 6. Produces & Inline Checks
51	
52	`produces` declares artifacts and checks beside the step that creates or attests them, using `astrid.verify` helpers: `file_nonempty`, `json_schema`, `json_file`, `audio_duration_min`, `image_dimensions`, and `all_of`. The gate runs checks after completion or ack; failure records the verifier output and rewinds the cursor. `passes_test` remains a normal `code` step. Sentinel-existence-only checks are rejected for non-trivial attested outputs.
53	
54	## 7. Gate Above Dispatch
55	
56	The gate checks: `active_run.json` exists; `plan.json` hash matches the pin; `events.jsonl` chain is intact; and the incoming command matches `plan[derived_cursor].command`. Any failure exits non-zero and prints one exact recovery command: start for missing active run, abort for integrity failure, or `astrid next --project <slug>` for command mismatch.
57	
58	Ordering is load-bearing. The first gate sits in `astrid/pipeline.py:15`; a defensive decorator re-checks at `astrid/core/orchestrator/runner.py:132`, the top of `run_orchestrator()`, before `_prepare_project_request()` at line 135 and `thread_wrapper.begin_orchestrator_run()` at line 136. Rejection writes zero project-run files. `events.jsonl` is the single task-mode provenance surface; `astrid/threads/wrapper.py:21-26` keeps existing thread env provenance in `runs/<id>/run.json`.
59	
60	## 8. Lifecycle Verbs
61	
62	Task-mode verbs extend top-level `astrid/pipeline.py:15`, not `astrid orchestrators`. Existing `astrid orchestrators run|list|inspect|validate` in `astrid/core/orchestrator/cli.py` stays unchanged.
63	
64	Agent mid-run verbs: `next`, `ack`, `status`, `abort`. Operator verbs: `start`, `abort`, `status`, `runs ls`. Author verbs: `author new`, `author check`, `author describe`, `author test`, `author compile`, `author explain`.
65	
66	## 9. Ack Decisions
67	
68	`approve` advances when the current step is awaiting approval and checks pass. `retry` is only valid after verifier failure and reruns with stderr/verifier output as feedback. `iterate --feedback` is only valid for `repeat.until=user_approves` and appends to cumulative constraints. `abort` ends the run. Attested steps require `--agent` or `--actor` as above; `--item <id>` targets one `repeat.for_each` item.
69	
70	## 10. Authoring
71	
72	`astrid.orchestrate` is the only committed representation for new task plans. `astrid author compile` writes gitignored `<pack>/build/<orch>.json`, and runtime hashes that compiled artifact. Pack additions are `<pack>/<orch>.py`, `<pack>/build/<orch>.json`, `<pack>/fixtures/<name>/`, and `<pack>/golden/<name>.events.jsonl`.
73	
74	`author check` is sub-second static validation: schema, references, nested plan resolution, semantic checks for non-trivial attested produces, sentinel-only rejection, and rejection of `code` argv to `astrid orchestrators run`. `author describe` prints the DAG. `author test --fixture` runs `--dry-run --auto-approve` and diffs `events.jsonl` against the fixture golden.

76	## 11. Stop-Hook Nudge
77	
78	V1 nudge is out-of-process and Claude Code only. A Stop hook runs `astrid next`; every `next` response includes the prohibition preamble verbatim, including repeated calls, so context decay is countered by re-injection.

181	## 15. Risk Register
182	
183	| Risk | Trigger | Mitigation |
184	| --- | --- | --- |
185	| Single-host assumption | No daemon means two operators can race. | Validate the chain before each command and print recovery commands. |
186	| Semantic verifier discipline | Authors regress to sentinel-existence checks. | `author check` rejects sentinel-only attested outputs. |
187	| Context-decay re-injection | Long sessions forget prohibitions. | Stop-hook nudge calls `next`; every response repeats the preamble. |
188	| Honor-model boundary | A malicious local agent edits files. | State plainly that hash chains are logs and tripwires, not sandboxing. |
189	| V1 infrastructure creep | A daemon, web server, HMAC, `.index.db`, or shared CAS is proposed as a shortcut. | Reject it for V1 and keep the design single-host, file-based, plain-hash, file-walk, and per-project. |
190	
191	## 16. Cut Points
192	
193	Phase 3 ships a useful frozen-plan runner: gate, three step kinds, produces checks, and repeat/fan-out. Phase 5 ships the author-friendly CLI surface. Phases 6-9 are polish and scale: nudge, CAS, inbox, and golden author tests.

203	- A7 Confirmed: the gate runs before both `_prepare_project_request()` and `thread_wrapper.begin_orchestrator_run()`, with zero project-run side effects on rejection.
204	- A8 Confirmed: root `.gitignore` excludes pack-local `<pack>/build/` outputs.
205	- A9 Confirmed: `ARTAGENTS_TASK_RUN_ID` is the inheritance env surface across orchestrator, executor, hype, project-run, and thread-wrapper code paths.

209	## Settled Decisions
210	
211	SD-001 three step kinds: Task mode has exactly `code`, `attested`, and `nested` so execution, evidence, and delegation stay distinct.
212	
213	SD-002 repeat body attributes: Iteration and fan-out are `repeat.until` and `repeat.for_each` body attributes so they apply uniformly to steps and nested bodies.
214	
215	SD-003 plan naming: Runtime uses immutable `plan.json` instead of checklist naming because the structure is a tree with nested bodies and loops.
216	
217	SD-004 event hash chain: `events.jsonl` uses plain `sha256(prev_hash + canonical_event_json)` with no HMAC because V1 needs an edit tripwire, not keyed tamper resistance.
218	
219	SD-005 no index database: V1 ships without `.index.db` because file walking and grep over `events.jsonl` are adequate until measured otherwise.
220	
221	SD-006 committed DSL: `astrid.orchestrate` Python DSL is the only committed authoring representation so source review happens in Python.
222	
223	SD-007 generated build JSON: `<pack>/build/<orch>.json` is gitignored and root `.gitignore` excludes pack build outputs because runtime pins generated artifacts.
224	
225	SD-008 per-project CAS: V1 uses only per-project `<slug>/.cas/<sha256>` storage because shared CAS adds coordination without current need.
226	
227	SD-009 code boundary: `code` is deterministic argv, a strict superset of `RUNTIME_KINDS={python,command}`, may target `astrid executors run <name>`, and must not target `astrid orchestrators run`.
228	
229	SD-010 nested boundary: Sub-orchestrator delegation is exclusively `nested` so the gate can hash and pin child structure.
230	
231	SD-011 gate checks: The gate validates active run presence, plan hash, event chain, and incoming command match before dispatch and prints the exact recovery command on rejection.
232	
233	SD-012 gate ordering: The gate runs before `_prepare_project_request()` and `thread_wrapper.begin_orchestrator_run()` so rejected commands create zero project-run side effects.
234	
235	SD-013 provenance surface: `events.jsonl` is the single write surface for task-mode provenance while thread provenance remains in `runs/<id>/run.json`.
236	
237	SD-014 lifecycle dispatch: Task-mode lifecycle verbs extend `astrid/pipeline.py:15` and the existing `astrid orchestrators` CLI remains unchanged.
238	
239	SD-015 task kernel namespace: New kernel modules live in `astrid/core/task/` to isolate gate, events, active-run, and env logic from legacy runners.
240	
241	SD-016 structure guardrails: `TOP_LEVEL_ARTAGENTS_DIRS` adds `orchestrate` and `verify`, with `tests/test_doctor_setup.py` updated so doctor accepts the new packages.
242	
243	SD-017 task run env: `ARTAGENTS_TASK_RUN_ID` is the integration surface for orchestrator, executor, and hype child calls to attach to the parent task run.
244	
245	SD-018 child output preservation: Task mode preserves child output dirs and mirrors hype artifacts under `runs/<task-run-id>/steps/<step-id>/produces/` while standalone behavior stays unchanged so `tests/test_project_runs.py` keeps passing.
246	
247	SD-019 attestor identity: Agent attestations require `--agent`, human attestations require `--actor` matching `ARTAGENTS_ACTOR`, and self-acks are rejected.
248	
249	SD-020 ack rules: `approve` advances, `retry` is only valid after verifier failure, `iterate --feedback` is only valid for `repeat.until=user_approves`, and `abort` ends the run.
250	
251	SD-021 inline produces checks: Produces inline checks replace verifier substeps while `passes_test` remains a normal `code` step.
252	
253	SD-022 semantic checks: `author check` rejects sentinel-only attested outputs because non-trivial artifacts need semantic validation.
254	
255	SD-023 stop-hook preamble: Every `astrid next` output includes the prohibition preamble verbatim because repeated injection fights context decay.
256	
257	SD-024 additive migration: Existing `OrchestratorDefinition` JSON manifests and `RUNTIME_KINDS={python,command}` keep working because V1 migration is additive.
258	
259	SD-025 honor model: V1 is single-host and honor-based with strong logging because it does not defend against malicious local agents.
260	
261	SD-026 cut points: Phase 3 is the frozen-plan runner ship point and Phase 5 is the author-friendly lifecycle ship point.
262	
263	SD-027 canonical migration: `astrid/packs/builtin/hype/` is the canonical migration example because it exercises the existing executor pipeline and additive pack layout.
264	
265	SD-028 phasing order: V1 implementation follows build phases 1-9 so kernel, step semantics, authoring, lifecycle, nudge, CAS, inbox, and golden tests land in dependency order.
266	
267	SD-029 V1 infrastructure limits: V1 excludes daemon, web server, HMAC/keyed crypto, `.index.db`, and shared CAS so the implementation stays file-based, inspectable, and additive.
268	
269	## Phase 1 status (kernel landed)
270	
271	Kernel modules under `astrid/core/task/`: `events.py`, `active_run.py`, `plan.py`, `env.py`, `gate.py`, `__init__.py`. Hash chain is plain `sha256(prev_hash + canonical_event_json(event))` per SD-004; no HMAC, no `.index.db`, no shared CAS (SD-029).
272	
273	Gate is decorated above dispatch at four entry points: `astrid/pipeline.py` (top-level `main`, fresh dispatch), and defensive reentry checks in `astrid/core/orchestrator/runner.py:run_orchestrator`, `astrid/core/executor/runner.py:run_executor`, and `astrid/packs/builtin/hype/run.py:main` — each placed strictly before `_prepare_project_request()` / `thread_wrapper.begin_orchestrator_run()` so a rejected command writes zero project-run files (SD-012).
274	
275	Three `prepare_project_run` callers (orchestrator runner, executor runner, hype direct entry) honor the env contract via the centralized branch inside `prepare_project_run` keyed on `is_in_task_run(slug)`; `ARTAGENTS_TASK_RUN_ID` / `ARTAGENTS_TASK_PROJECT` / `ARTAGENTS_TASK_STEP_ID` redirect run output under `<projects_root>/<slug>/runs/<task-run-id>/steps/<step-id>/` and suppress child `run.json` / cumulative `runs.json` writes; hype artifacts mirror under `<step_dir>/produces/` (SD-018). `ARTAGENTS_TASK_STEP_ID` is a Phase 1-introduced sibling env var the design doc names alongside `ARTAGENTS_TASK_RUN_ID`. `command_for_argv(argv)` produces the canonical command-string form that authored `plan.json` step commands must match exactly, including the `--project <slug>` token.
276	
277	Recovery strings are emitted verbatim per SD-011 (`astrid abort --project <slug>` for active-run / plan-hash / chain / exhausted; `astrid next --project <slug>` for off-cursor), even though those verbs ship in Phase 5.
278	
279	Deferred: full subprocess env propagation into child code-step launchers (Phase 2; Phase 1 only ships the `child_subprocess_env()` helper used by the e2e smoke); lifecycle verbs `astrid next` / `abort` / `approve` / `retry` / `iterate` (Phase 5); per-project CAS at `<slug>/.cas/<sha256>` (Phase 7, SD-008). New step kinds (`code`, `attested`, `nested`), produces inline checks, and the Python authoring DSL all remain out of Phase 1 scope.

# Project-execution review of `idea.md`

## 1. Sprint sequencing in practice — go serial

The doc claims Sprint 1 and 2 can run in partial parallel because "only `status` output formatting overlaps." That's true on paper and wrong in practice for one developer.

The two sprints share more than `status`: both touch `attach`, both touch `project.json`, both write the *contract* the rest of the system reads ("what is bound right now?"). Sprint 2's default-timeline pointer is *consumed* by Sprint 1's attach. Holding two evolving contracts in your head while also debugging concurrent-write edge cases on `events.jsonl` is exactly the cognitive load that produces subtle bugs in the foundation everything else depends on.

Recommendation: **strict serial, 1 → 2 → 3 → 4a → 4b**. Lose ~1 week of wall-clock; gain a clean foundation. You also get the dogfooding benefit (see Q5): Sprint 1 can be in active personal use for two weeks before Sprint 2 starts, which is the cheapest QA you'll ever buy.

## 2. Pre-Sprint-1 prerequisites

Before a single line of Sprint 1 code:

- **Snapshot `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/astrid-projects/`** to a timestamped tarball. The plan does three one-shot migrations across sprints; you need a known-good rollback point per sprint, not just per project.
- **Branch strategy:** one long-lived `reshape/` branch with sprint sub-branches (`reshape/sprint-1-sessions` etc.) merged into it; don't merge to `main` until 4a ships green. Tag `pre-reshape` on `main` first.
- **Spike: locking primitive choice.** Decide between `fcntl.flock` and a `.lock` sidecar file *before* Sprint 1, not during. macOS-only is fine; document it. 1-day spike.
- **Spike: env inheritance audit.** The doc lists this as a Sprint 1 deliverable but it's actually a precondition — if `ASTRID_SESSION_ID` doesn't survive the executor runner, the whole binding contract is fiction. Audit `astrid/core/executor/runner.py` and `astrid/threads/wrapper.py` first, half a day.
- **Test fixture: a "frozen" projects directory** committed under `tests/fixtures/projects-pre-reshape/` representing the pre-migration on-disk shape. Every migration script gets a golden test against it.
- **Decision log file** (`docs/reshape/decisions.md`) seeded with the load-bearing decisions from `idea.md` lines 49–69, so when you're three weeks in and wonder "why did I make slugs mutable again?" the answer is one file away.
- **Kill the current Phase 1 kernel work** mentally. The orchestrator-v1-plan kernel landed `events.py`, `gate.py`, `active_run.py` — Sprint 1 will rewrite chunks of these. Don't pretend continuity; declare a clean reset and migrate forward.

## 3. Sprint-entry briefing ritual

Each sprint kickoff (or context-window resume) is the same five-step recipe:

1. **Re-read `idea.md` Foundation section + the upcoming sprint section only.** Not the prior sprints. They're done; their decisions are in code.
2. **Read the sprint-exit deliverables of the *previous* sprint** (see Q4) — schema diff, runbook, fixtures.
3. **Read the relevant existing files** the sprint will touch (Sprint 1 = `astrid/core/task/{events,active_run,gate,env}.py`, `astrid/threads/wrapper.py`; Sprint 2 = `astrid/core/project/`, existing `timeline.json` schema; Sprint 3 = `astrid/core/task/{plan,inbox,lifecycle}.py`).
4. **Run the existing test suite green on the snapshot fixture** before touching code. If anything is red, fix it or quarantine it before starting; don't carry red tests into a foundation rewrite.
5. **Write the sprint's golden test fixtures first.** For Sprint 1: a multi-tab race scenario as a pytest. For Sprint 3: a plan-mutation-during-dispatch fixture. Failing-test-first is the kickoff act.

After context reset mid-sprint, the same recipe but with one addition: re-read the in-progress sprint's `WIP-NOTES.md` (a scratchpad you maintain inside the sprint branch — invariants you've discovered, dead ends you've ruled out).

## 4. Sprint-exit deliverables that aren't code

Each sprint produces, *as part of "done"*:

- **Schema diff** — a `docs/reshape/sprint-N-schema.md` showing before/after on every on-disk file shape touched. Sprint 2's reader of Sprint 1's `lease.json` deserves better than reading code to find the field names.
- **Migration runbook** — exact commands the user (you) runs to migrate, in order, with checkpoints. "Snapshot. Run script. Verify N projects, M timelines. Spot-check one project's `status`. Commit migration log."
- **Updated SKILL.md sections** — see Q9. Not a separate task; a merge-blocker.
- **Golden test fixtures** — committed into `tests/fixtures/sprint-N/`. Sprint 4a's hype port doesn't have to re-derive the expected event sequence for a basic run; Sprint 3 leaves it.
- **Decision log entries** for any decision *not* already in `idea.md` that came up during implementation. Inevitable; capture them.
- **Sprint review note** — one page: what shipped, what slipped, what surprised you, what the next sprint should know. Five minutes to write, hours to recover later if skipped.

## 5. Dogfooding cadence — start at end of Sprint 1

Sprint 1 ships sessions, status, attach, identity. As soon as it merges, *use it for everything Astrid-related you do, including building Sprint 2*. This is the early-warning system for whether the binding contract is actually usable. Two weeks of you-yourself bouncing off `astrid status says no session, but I'm clearly in a project` will surface UX gaps that no test catches.

Sprint 2 dogfooded during Sprint 3. Sprint 3 dogfooded during 4a. By 4a you're using the new model to port hype, which is the strongest possible adversarial test of the new model.

The doc never explicitly schedules dogfooding; this is the single biggest project-management gap.

## 6. De-risking the hype port — yes, do a Sprint-3 spike

The doc names hype as the riskiest single deliverable and isolates it in 4a. Good. But waiting until 4a to discover schema gaps is too late — if the step model is wrong, you've already shipped Sprint 3's migration.

Add a **Sprint 3 mid-point spike: throwaway hype-port-of-one-stage**. Pick `transcribe → cut` (two steps, one local adapter, one produces-check). Hand-write the `plan.json`, run it through the new kernel, ack through it. Do *not* productionize. Goal: surface schema/adapter/mutation/inbox gaps while Sprint 3 is still molten.

Budget: 2 days inside Sprint 3. If gaps surface, fix them in Sprint 3, not 4a. This is cheap insurance.

## 7. Migration choreography

Three one-shot migrations: Sprint 1 (active_run + threads → sessions), Sprint 2 (timeline.json → timelines/<ulid>/), Sprint 3 (steps → versioned, plan.json → collapsed schema).

Safe ordering:

- Each sprint's migration is **idempotent and self-contained**: Sprint 2 reads a post-Sprint-1 disk; Sprint 3 reads a post-Sprint-2 disk. Don't combine.
- Each sprint ships its migration *first* (day 1 of sprint), against the *previous* sprint's snapshot, then builds new code on the migrated shape. Migrating last is how you ship a runtime that doesn't match real on-disk state.
- **Snapshot before each migration**, tarball'd with sprint+date. `astrid-projects-pre-sprint2-20260601.tar.gz`.
- Migration N+1 conflict risk: Sprint 3 changes `steps/<id>/` to `steps/<id>/v1/`. Sprint 2's `timelines/<ulid>/manifest.json` references runs which reference steps. Sprint 3's migration must update those references too — which means Sprint 2's manifest schema must record step references as `(run_id, step_id)`, not as paths. Lock that in Sprint 2.
- **Migration script is itself a step** (eat the dogfood): `astrid plan add-step --command 'astrid migrate sprint-3' --produces migration-log.json`. Audit trail of your own migration.

## 8. First-run experience after Sprint 1

The 60-second walkthrough today, after Sprint 1 ships and before Sprint 2:

```
$ astrid status
ERROR: no agent identity. Run: astrid identity init --agent-id <slug>
$ astrid identity init --agent-id claude-1
$ astrid status
no session. no projects exist yet.
suggested: astrid projects create <name>
$ astrid projects create demo
created project demo (ulid: 01J...)
$ astrid attach demo
attached session 01J... → project demo
no timeline (sprint 2). no run.
$ astrid start builtin.hype -- ...
```

What's missing to make this work without dead-ends:

- **`astrid projects create` must work without a session.** The CLI gate exempts it (the doc says so) — verify in Sprint 1 acceptance.
- **`astrid identity init` verb** — the doc says "first-run bootstrap prompts the user" but doesn't list the verb. Add it explicitly to Sprint 1 deliverables.
- **`astrid status` when zero projects exist** must offer the create suggestion, not just say "no session" — that's a dead-end UX.
- **Post-migration first run**: if migration ran, `status` should print "migrated N projects from pre-Sprint-1 shape; default project: <slug> (override with `astrid attach <other>`)". This bridges the gap between "everything was just rewritten" and "what do I do now."
- **Timeline-less attach during Sprint 1** — Sprint 2 hasn't shipped, so `--timeline` is a no-op. Document this in `status` output ("timelines arrive in Sprint 2; run-as-timeline-proxy for now").

## 9. Documentation as a deliverable — written before merge, opinionated

SKILL.md and AGENTS.md are not cleanup. They are **the agent's runtime contract**. If they're stale, the agent — including future-you using Claude Code on this repo — will issue old verbs against new state and clobber things.

Hard rule: **the SKILL.md / AGENTS.md diff for a sprint must be in the same PR as the code.** Not a follow-up. Not a "I'll update docs at the end." A merge that ships new verbs without telling the agent what they are is a regression.

Concretely: every sprint has a checklist item "SKILL.md updated to reflect new verbs and removed verbs; AGENTS.md cross-references updated; stop-hook preamble re-rendered." PR is blocked until that line is checked.

The doc currently lists "SKILL.md / AGENTS.md rewritten" only inside Sprint 1 deliverables. Replicate this into Sprints 2, 3, 4a, 4b.

## 10. What this plan is missing at the project-management level

- **No risk register.** The orchestrator-v1-plan doc had one (Section 15). `idea.md` doesn't. Inherit and extend it: hype-port risk, migration-conflict risk, lock-correctness risk, single-developer context-loss risk, Reigh-app schema-divergence risk (timeline.json mirrors reigh-app's TimelineConfig — what happens if reigh-app changes shape mid-reshape?).
- **No rollback plan.** "Snapshot before each migration" is half of one. The other half: "if Sprint N is in production for X days and a critical bug surfaces, the rollback is: stop using astrid CLI for live work, re-checkout pre-sprint-N tag, restore tarball, lose work since." Write it down explicitly per sprint so you don't have to invent it under pressure.
- **No decision log.** See Q2 prerequisites. Without one, a Sprint 4 question of "wait, why is `requires_ack` not on group steps?" becomes an archaeology project.
- **No definition of "done" per sprint.** "Ship state" paragraphs are good but informal. Convert each sprint's ship state into 3–5 explicit acceptance criteria you can check off. Sprint 1: "two tabs in same project cannot both write to the same run; takeover correctly fences the loser; status shows the binding from any tab; identity is required."
- **No sprint review ritual.** Even solo, end each sprint with: re-read the sprint section in `idea.md`, mark deliverables shipped/deferred, write the sprint review note (Q4), commit it. This is how you avoid week-7 amnesia.
- **No explicit "freeze period" before 4a.** Sprint 4a is the keystone. Add a 2-3 day stabilization window between Sprint 3 merge and Sprint 4a kickoff: no new work, only fixing whatever Sprint 3 dogfooding has surfaced. The doc treats "Sprint 3 ships, Sprint 4a starts Monday" as continuous — it shouldn't be.
- **No external-dependency surfacing.** Reigh-app's `TimelineConfig` shape, RunPod artifact-fetch semantics, pyenv 3.11.11 pin, Remotion env var — all loadbearing externals scattered across SKILL.md. A `docs/reshape/external-deps.md` with versions and contact points (even if it's just "you, ask future-you") makes the soak weeks before 4b less surprising.

# Project-execution review: Astrid reshape

## 1. Sprint sequencing in practice — go serial

**Recommendation: serial. Drop the parallel framing entirely.**

The doc's "1 and 2 in parallel" optimism is fictional for one developer. The only thing that's literally parallel is "two branches existing at once" — but a single brain can't hold both the session/lease/CAS write path *and* the timelines-as-containers schema migration in working memory without one polluting the other. Worse: Sprint 2 needs to consume `project.json`'s default-timeline pointer, which Sprint 1 introduces. That's a sequencing dependency hiding in the parallel claim — doing them concurrently means stubbing the pointer in 2, then revisiting once 1 lands. Net cost > net savings.

Where you can compress: Sprint 2 is the smallest of the four (timelines schema is mostly file-shuffling and a manifest type). Run 1 → 2 strictly serial, but treat Sprint 2 as a 1.5-week sprint, not 2. That recovers your wall-clock budget honestly. Total honest budget: **10–12 weeks**, not 8.

The one thing worth doing "in parallel" with Sprint 1 is **documentation drafting** (see #9) — writing the new SKILL.md flow before code makes the surface concrete.

## 2. Pre-Sprint-1 prerequisites (Sprint 0, ~3 days)

Concrete checklist before writing a line of Sprint 1 code:

- **Snapshot `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/astrid-projects/` to a tarball** stored outside the repo, dated. This is your migration rollback. Re-snapshot at the start of every sprint.
- **Inventory script** (read-only): walk every project, list every `active_run.json`, every per-run `timeline.json`, every `plan.json`, every thread state file. Output a CSV. This is your migration test fixture and your "did we miss any" check.
- **Branch strategy**: long-lived `reshape/` branch off main; one feature branch per sprint merged to `reshape/`; `reshape/` only merges to main after Sprint 4a soak. Don't try to ship reshape sprints to main incrementally — half-migrated state on disk will bite.
- **A two-tab adversarial test harness**: literally a script that opens two shells and races the same verb. You'll need this to validate Sprint 1's lease epoch end-to-end and you do not want to be writing it under pressure.
- **Spike: env inheritance audit** (the doc lists this as a Sprint 1 deliverable; promote it to Sprint 0). Confirm `ASTRID_SESSION_ID` survives every existing subprocess path before designing around it. If something scrubs env, Sprint 1's design changes.
- **Spike: flock semantics on macOS APFS** for `events.jsonl`. The whole CAS story relies on `flock` being honest. Twenty lines of test code, but you want this proven before you build on it.
- **Pin a "production" workload**: pick one specific past hype run (transcript + brief + final mp4) you'll re-run end-to-end as the regression gate at every sprint exit.

## 3. Sprint-entry briefing ritual

Each sprint, before the first commit, the developer (or fresh-context agent) does a fixed warm-up:

1. **Re-read `idea.md` Foundation section** (the load-bearing decisions). These don't change between sprints; the agent keeps forgetting them.
2. **Read the prior sprint's exit handoff** (see #4) — schema diff, changelog, runbook.
3. **Re-run the inventory script** from Sprint 0. Diff against last run. If on-disk shape moved unexpectedly, stop and reconcile.
4. **Read the sprint's own decisions block** out loud (literally — verbalize what's locked vs. what's open).
5. **Mock the exit state**: write the `astrid status` output you expect to see at the end of this sprint, by hand, in a scratch file. This is the contract. If you can't write it, you don't understand the sprint yet.
6. **Check the snapshot is fresh** (re-tar projects dir).

After context window resets mid-sprint: re-load steps 1, 2, and 5. The "mocked exit state" file is the cheapest re-anchor.

## 4. Sprint-exit deliverables that aren't code

Each sprint must produce, in a `docs/reshape/sprint-N/` folder:

- **CHANGELOG.md** — verbs added, verbs removed, on-disk paths added/moved/deleted, env vars introduced.
- **schema-diff.md** — before/after for every JSON shape touched.
- **migration-runbook.md** — exact commands run, exact failure modes seen, exact rollback steps. Written *during* the migration, not after.
- **SKILL.md / AGENTS.md patch** — the doc surface for the new verbs (see #9).
- **golden test fixture** — at least one frozen `events.jsonl` for the new event types, used for regression.
- **known-bugs.md** — a short list of "we know this is broken / deferred" so the next sprint doesn't rediscover them.
- **One-paragraph "what would I do differently"** — for your own future self.

If a sprint ships without these, the next sprint pays double.

## 5. Dogfooding cadence — start at Sprint 2 ship, mandatory by Sprint 3

Sprint 1 is too thin to dogfood (no timelines, no plan editing — you're just attaching). Sprint 2 ships timelines and final outputs; **start dogfooding the moment Sprint 2's exit is signed**. That means: do Sprint 3 development *itself* as Astrid runs against an Astrid project named `reshape-sprint-3`. Every meaningful action (a spike, a script, a port attempt) is `astrid plan add-step`. This will be uncomfortable and slow at first; that's the point — friction you feel here is friction every user feels.

By Sprint 4a (the hype port), dogfooding is non-negotiable. The hype port itself should be tracked as a run in the new system. If you can't track your own port-of-hype work as Astrid steps, the model isn't ready.

## 6. De-risking the keystone: hype port

**Yes, do a throwaway hype port spike in Sprint 3 — explicitly budgeted as a Sprint 3 deliverable, not a Sprint 4a preview.**

Concretely: in the back half of Sprint 3, take the *first three steps of hype only* (transcribe → cut → render) and port them against the new step model. Don't ship it; don't merge it. The deliverable is a `docs/reshape/sprint-3/hype-spike-findings.md` that lists every schema gap, adapter mismatch, and cost-field ambiguity discovered. Then revise the Sprint 3 schema *while it's still cheap*.

Without this spike, Sprint 4a will discover the gaps *after* the schema is locked, and you'll either ship a band-aid or slip a sprint. The spike costs maybe 2 days; it buys 2+ weeks of insurance.

## 7. Migration choreography

Three on-disk migrations (Sprint 1: active_run + threads; Sprint 2: timeline.json reshape; Sprint 3: plan.json + versioned step paths). Safe ordering:

- Each migration is **a single script**, idempotent, with a `--dry-run` default and `--apply` flag, that writes a per-project audit log.
- **Snapshot before, snapshot after.** Both go in the runbook.
- **One project at a time** — never bulk-migrate. Pick the smallest project first; rehearse on a *copy*; run on the real one; verify with the inventory script; then move to the next.
- Conflicts between migration N and N+1: the data shape after migration N is the *input contract* for migration N+1. Write a frozen sample of that intermediate shape into `tests/fixtures/post-sprint-N/` so Sprint N+1's migration script has a regression target. If Sprint N+1's migration breaks on real data that doesn't match the frozen sample, you have a data-shape drift bug to diagnose, not a migration bug.
- Sprint 3's versioned-step-path migration (`steps/<id>/` → `steps/<id>/v1/`) is the riskiest because of path depth. Rehearse twice.

## 8. First-run experience after Sprint 1

Walk-through of the broken case: user opens a fresh tab post-Sprint-1, has just had everything migrated, types `astrid status`. Status correctly says "no session." User types `astrid attach` — needs a project. Default project is set, but no project actually exists yet because… wait, they were migrated, so projects do exist. Good. But the *default* pointer in `~/.astrid/config.json` was never set (that's a bootstrap step nothing in Sprint 1 owns).

Gaps Sprint 1 must explicitly close:

- **First-run bootstrap verb** that runs when `~/.astrid/identity.json` is missing: prompts for `agent_id`, scans `astrid-projects/` for existing projects, offers to set one as default, writes both files. Without this, the agent's first 60 seconds is "error, error, error."
- **`astrid status` when unbound and no default**: must list discoverable projects with an explicit "run `astrid attach <slug>` to begin." Not just "no session." The doc says status suggests defaults — make sure "no defaults yet" is also a designed UX, not an error.
- **Migration script must set the per-project default-timeline pointer to a sentinel** (even though Sprint 2 wires it). Otherwise Sprint 2's migration has to backfill across the entire project tree.

## 9. Documentation as a deliverable

**Opinion: SKILL.md / AGENTS.md sections get rewritten *before* code merge for that sprint, and the rewrite is the acceptance test.**

Concretely: a sprint is not "done" until the SKILL.md section describing its new verbs is written *and* a fresh-context agent can follow it through one full task without asking the human a clarifying question. If the doc requires a clarifying question, the verb's UX is wrong, not the doc.

Why before merge: documentation written after-the-fact rationalizes whatever you built. Documentation written against the verb design surfaces awkwardness while it's still cheap to fix the verb. The doc is the spec.

Practically: each sprint has a "doc PR" merged immediately before or with the code PR. Never lag.

## 10. What this plan is missing at the project-management level

Load-bearing things no sprint covers:

- **Decision log.** Every locked decision in `idea.md` should have a one-line entry in `docs/reshape/decisions.md` with date and the alternative rejected. When (not if) a sprint discovers a locked decision was wrong, you need the audit trail to revisit it deliberately.
- **Risk register, kept live.** The doc names risks implicitly. Promote them to a tracked list with current mitigation status. Top entries: hype port complexity, flock semantics under load, env inheritance regressions, migration data loss.
- **Rollback plan per sprint.** "Restore from snapshot" is a rollback for data; what's the rollback for the *code*? Each sprint exit should specify: which commit to revert to, how to detect we should revert, what's the user-visible signal.
- **Sprint review ritual.** Even solo: one fixed hour at the end of each sprint, with the question "did the ship-state claim in `idea.md` actually hold?" Document gap; feed into next sprint's brief.
- **Soak-week explicit calendar slot between 4a and 4b.** The doc gates 4b on "one clean week of hype runs" — that week needs to be a planned, *non-coding* slot, not "the gap before I get bored." Schedule it. Use it to dogfood, fix small papercuts, write docs.
- **Stop-line: "if X, halt and rethink."** Pre-commit to halting conditions. E.g. "if the hype port spike (Sprint 3 #6) reveals that plan-template materialization can't express hype's dynamic discovery, halt Sprint 3 before locking the schema." Without pre-committed stop-lines, sunk-cost momentum carries you past the off-ramp.
- **A "one verb per session" rule for the developer during Sprints 3 and 4a.** Cognitive load cap. The reshape touches the kernel; a session that introduces three verbs at once is a session that produces three half-tested verbs.

65	        current_size_gb = volume_info.get("size", 0)
66	        if current_size_gb >= 100:
67	            return {
68	                "ok": True,
69	                "expanded": False,
70	                "current_size_gb": current_size_gb,
71	                "target_size_gb": current_size_gb,
72	                "message": f"Storage '{label}' has adequate capacity ({current_size_gb} GB)",
73	            }
74	
75	        target_size_gb = current_size_gb + min_free_gb
76	        expanded = _expand_network_volume(api_key, volume_id, target_size_gb)
77	        return {
78	            "ok": True,
79	            "expanded": expanded,
80	            "current_size_gb": current_size_gb,
81	            "target_size_gb": target_size_gb,
82	            "message": (
83	                f"Expanded storage '{label}' to {target_size_gb} GB"
84	                if expanded
85	                else f"Expansion failed for storage '{label}', continuing anyway"
86	            ),
87	        }
88	    except Exception as exc:
89	        return {
90	            "ok": True,
91	            "expanded": False,
92	            "current_size_gb": None,
93	            "target_size_gb": None,
94	            "message": f"Error checking storage space: {exc}",
95	        }
96	
97	
98	def get_storage_volume_id(api_key: str, storage_name: str | None) -> str | None:
99	    """Resolve a storage volume name to its RunPod network volume ID."""
100	    if not storage_name:
101	        return None
102	
103	    volumes = get_network_volumes(api_key)
104	    for volume in volumes:
105	        if volume.get("name") == storage_name:
106	            return volume.get("id")
107	    return None
108	
109	
110	def _parse_size(size_value: str) -> int:
111	    normalized = size_value.strip()
112	    if normalized.endswith("T"):
113	        return int(float(normalized[:-1]) * 1024)
114	    if normalized.endswith("G"):
115	        return int(float(normalized[:-1]))
116	    if normalized.endswith("M"):
117	        return int(float(normalized[:-1]) / 1024)
118	    if normalized.endswith("K"):
119	        return 0
120	    return int(float(normalized))
121	
122	
123	def parse_df_output(raw_output: str) -> dict[str, int]:
124	    """Parse the `/workspace` `df` output into normalized GiB values."""
125	    parsed = {
126	        "total_gb": 0,
127	        "used_gb": 0,
128	        "free_gb": 0,
129	        "percent_used": 0,
130	    }
131	
132	    for line in raw_output.splitlines():
133	        stripped = line.strip()
134	        if "===" in stripped or "/workspace" not in stripped:
135	            continue
136	
137	        parts = stripped.split()
138	        if len(parts) < 5:
139	            continue
140	
141	        try:
142	            parsed["total_gb"] = _parse_size(parts[1])
143	            parsed["used_gb"] = _parse_size(parts[2])
144	            parsed["free_gb"] = _parse_size(parts[3])
145	            parsed["percent_used"] = int(parts[4].rstrip("%"))
146	            break
147	        except (ValueError, IndexError):
148	            continue
149	
150	    return parsed
151	
152	
153	def evaluate_storage_health(
154	    parsed: dict[str, int],
155	    api_total_gb: int | None,
156	    min_free_gb: int,
157	    max_percent_used: int,
158	) -> dict[str, Any]:
159	    """Evaluate parsed storage metrics and decide whether expansion is needed."""
160	    del api_total_gb
161	    free_gb = parsed.get("free_gb", 0)
162	    percent_used = parsed.get("percent_used", 0)
163	
164	    if percent_used >= max_percent_used:
165	        return {
166	            "healthy": False,
167	            "needs_expansion": True,
168	            "message": f"CRITICAL: {percent_used}% used, only {free_gb}GB free!",
169	        }
170	    if free_gb < min_free_gb:
171	        return {
172	            "healthy": False,
173	            "needs_expansion": True,
174	            "message": f"LOW SPACE: Only {free_gb}GB free (need {min_free_gb}GB)",
175	        }
176	    return {
177	        "healthy": True,
178	        "needs_expansion": False,
179	        "message": f"OK: {free_gb}GB free ({100 - percent_used}% available)",
180	    }
181	
182

186	    "check_and_expand_storage",
187	    "evaluate_storage_health",
188	    "get_storage_volume_id",

190	]

1	"""Async facade for interacting with a single RunPod pod lifecycle."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import asyncio
6	import logging
7	import os
8	import time
9	from typing import Any
10	
11	from . import api
12	from .config import RunPodConfig
13	from .errors import LaunchFailure, NotReadyTimeout, SSHError, TerminateError
14	from .events import EventHooks, PodState, _emit_error, _emit_state
15	from .ssh import SSHClient
16	from .storage import STORAGE_CHECK_COMMAND, evaluate_storage_health, parse_df_output
17	
18	logger = logging.getLogger("runpod_lifecycle.pod")
19	
20	
21	class Pod:
22	    """Async operations for a specific RunPod pod."""
23	
24	    def __init__(
25	        self,
26	        pod_id: str,
27	        name: str,
28	        config: RunPodConfig,
29	        hooks: EventHooks | None = None,
30	        ram_tier: int = 0,
31	        storage_volume: str | None = None,
32	    ) -> None:
33	        self.id = pod_id
34	        self.name = name
35	        self.config = config
36	        self.hooks = hooks or EventHooks()
37	        self._ram_tier = ram_tier
38	        self._storage_volume = storage_volume
39	        self._ssh_details: dict[str, Any] | None = None
40	        self._last_exec_at: float | None = None
41	        self._created_at = time.monotonic()
42	
43	    async def wait_ready(self, timeout: int = 600) -> dict[str, Any]:
44	        start_time = time.monotonic()
45	        poll_interval = 5
46	        current_state: PodState | None = None
47	
48	        while True:
49	            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
50	            if elapsed > timeout:
51	                raise NotReadyTimeout(f"Pod {self.id} did not become ready within {timeout} seconds")
52	
53	            status = await self.status()
54	            desired_status = status.get("desired_status") if status else None
55	            ports = (status.get("ports") or []) if status else []
56	
57	            if current_state is None:
58	                current_state = PodState.PROVISIONING
59	                await _emit_state(self.hooks, self.id, PodState.PROVISIONING, {"status": status or {}})
60	
61	            if desired_status in {"FAILED", "TERMINATED"}:
62	                failed_state = PodState.TERMINATED if desired_status == "TERMINATED" else PodState.FAILED
63	                await _emit_state(self.hooks, self.id, failed_state, {"status": status or {}})
64	                raise LaunchFailure(f"Pod {self.id} entered terminal state {desired_status}")
65	
66	            has_ssh_port = any(port.get("privatePort") == 22 for port in ports)
67	            if desired_status == "RUNNING" and has_ssh_port:
68	                if current_state is not PodState.READY:
69	                    self._ssh_details = await self._ensure_ssh_details()
70	                    current_state = PodState.READY
71	                    await _emit_state(self.hooks, self.id, PodState.READY, {"status": status})
72	                return status
73	
74	            if current_state is not PodState.STARTING:
75	                current_state = PodState.STARTING
76	                await _emit_state(self.hooks, self.id, PodState.STARTING, {"status": status or {}})
77	
78	            await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)
79	
80	    async def status(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
81	        return await asyncio.to_thread(api.get_pod_status, self.id, self.config.api_key)
82	
83	    async def exec_ssh(self, cmd: str, timeout: int = 600) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
84	        ssh_details = await self._ensure_ssh_details()
85	        ssh_client = self._build_ssh_client(ssh_details)
86	
87	        def _run_command() -> tuple[int, str, str]:
88	            ssh_client.connect()
89	            try:
90	                return ssh_client.execute_command(cmd, timeout)
91	            finally:
92	                ssh_client.disconnect()
93	
94	        try:
95	            result = await asyncio.to_thread(_run_command)
96	        except Exception as exc:
97	            raise SSHError(f"SSH command failed for pod {self.id}: {exc}") from exc
98	
99	        self._last_exec_at = time.monotonic()
100	        return result
101	
102	    async def is_idle(self, threshold_seconds: int) -> bool:
103	        last_activity = self._last_exec_at or self._created_at
104	        if time.monotonic() - last_activity < threshold_seconds:
105	            return False
106	
107	        try:
108	            exit_code, stdout, _stderr = await self.exec_ssh(
109	                "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits"
110	            )
111	            if exit_code != 0:
112	                return False
113	
114	            first_line = stdout.strip().splitlines()[0]
115	            return int(first_line) < 5
116	        except (IndexError, ValueError, SSHError) as exc:
117	            logger.warning("Could not determine GPU utilization for pod %s: %s", self.id, exc)
118	            return False
119	
120	    async def terminate(self) -> None:
121	        try:
122	            await asyncio.to_thread(api.terminate_pod, self.id, self.config.api_key)
123	        except Exception as exc:
124	            await _emit_error(self.hooks, exc, {"pod_id": self.id})
125	            raise TerminateError(f"Failed to terminate pod {self.id}: {exc}") from exc
126	
127	        await _emit_state(self.hooks, self.id, PodState.TERMINATED, {"pod_id": self.id})
128	
129	    async def check_storage_health(
130	        self,
131	        min_free_gb: int = 50,
132	        max_percent_used: int = 85,
133	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
134	        _exit_code, raw_output, _stderr = await self.exec_ssh(STORAGE_CHECK_COMMAND, timeout=30)
135	        parsed = parse_df_output(raw_output)
136	
137	        api_total_gb = None
138	        if self._storage_volume:
139	            volumes = await asyncio.to_thread(api.get_network_volumes, self.config.api_key)

141	            api_total_gb = volume_info.get("size") if volume_info else None
142	
143	        return evaluate_storage_health(parsed, api_total_gb, min_free_gb, max_percent_used)

146	        """Open and return the underlying connected paramiko SSH client."""
147	        ssh_details = self._ensure_ssh_details_sync()
148	        ssh_client = self._build_ssh_client(ssh_details)
149	        ssh_client.connect()
150	        raw_client = getattr(ssh_client, "client", None)
151	        if raw_client is None:
152	            raise SSHError(f"SSH client for pod {self.id} did not expose a raw client")
153	        return raw_client

26	def _parse_duration(text: str) -> int:
27	    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d+)\s*([smhd]?)\s*", text)
28	    if not m:
29	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid duration: {text!r}")
30	    n, unit = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2) or "s"
31	    return n * {"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600, "d": 86400}[unit]

45	def _print_table(rows: list[list[str]], headers: list[str]) -> None:
46	    if not rows:

48	        return
49	    widths = [max(len(h), *(len(r[i]) for r in rows)) for i, h in enumerate(headers)]
50	    fmt = "  ".join(f"{{:<{w}}}" for w in widths)
51	    print(fmt.format(*headers))
52	    print(fmt.format(*["-" * w for w in widths]))
53	    for r in rows:

146	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
147	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="runpod-lifecycle", description="RunPod pod lifecycle CLI.")
148	    parser.add_argument("--api-key", help="Override RUNPOD_API_KEY env var.")
149	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
150	
151	    p_list = sub.add_parser("list", help="List all pods on the account.")
152	    p_list.add_argument("--name-prefix", help="Filter to pods whose name starts with PREFIX.")
153	    p_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
154	
155	    p_status = sub.add_parser("status", help="Show normalized status for a pod.")
156	    p_status.add_argument("pod_id")
157	
158	    p_term = sub.add_parser("terminate", help="Terminate a pod.")
159	    p_term.add_argument("pod_id")
160	    p_term.add_argument("--yes", "-y", action="store_true", help="Skip confirmation.")
161	
162	    p_orph = sub.add_parser("find-orphans", help="Find pods on the account not in the supplied known-ids list.")
163	    p_orph.add_argument("--known-ids-file", help="File with one pod id per line. Empty if omitted.")
164	    p_orph.add_argument("--older-than", type=_parse_duration, default=None,
165	                        help="Only orphans with uptime >= this duration (e.g. 1h, 30m, 90s).")
166	    p_orph.add_argument("--name-prefix", help="Filter pods to those whose name starts with PREFIX.")
167	    p_orph.add_argument("--terminate", action="store_true", help="After listing, terminate each orphan.")
168	    p_orph.add_argument("--yes", "-y", action="store_true", help="Skip terminate confirmation.")
169	
170	    p_gpu = sub.add_parser("gpu-types", help="List available GPU types from RunPod.")
171	    p_gpu.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
172	
173	    return parser
174	
175	
176	_HANDLERS = {
177	    "list": _cmd_list,
178	    "status": _cmd_status,
179	    "terminate": _cmd_terminate,
180	    "find-orphans": _cmd_find_orphans,
181	    "gpu-types": _cmd_gpu_types,
182	}
183	
184	
185	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
186	    load_dotenv()
187	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
188	    handler = _HANDLERS[args.cmd]
189	    try:
190	        return asyncio.run(handler(args))
191	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
192	        return 130
193	    except Exception as exc:
194	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
195	        return 1
196	
197	
198	if __name__ == "__main__":
199	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""Account-wide RunPod discovery, attach-by-id, orphan detection, and module-level termination."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import asyncio
6	import logging
7	from dataclasses import dataclass
8	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable
9	
10	from . import api
11	from .config import RunPodConfig
12	from .errors import LaunchFailure, TerminateError
13	from .events import EventHooks, PodState, _emit_error, _emit_state
14	from .pod import Pod
15	
16	logger = logging.getLogger("runpod_lifecycle.discovery")
17	
18	
19	@dataclass(frozen=True)
20	class PodSummary:
21	    id: str
22	    name: str | None
23	    desired_status: str | None
24	    actual_status: str | None
25	    gpu_type: str | None
26	    image: str | None
27	    created_at: str | None
28	    cost_per_hr: float
29	    uptime_seconds: int | None
30	    ports: list[dict[str, Any]]
31	    network_volume_id: str | None
32	
33	
34	def _to_summary(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> PodSummary:
35	    runtime = raw.get("runtime") if isinstance(raw.get("runtime"), dict) else {}
36	    machine = raw.get("machine") if isinstance(raw.get("machine"), dict) else {}
37	    cost = raw.get("costPerHr")
38	    try:
39	        cost_val = float(cost) if cost is not None else 0.0
40	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
41	        cost_val = 0.0
42	    return PodSummary(
43	        id=str(raw.get("id") or ""),
44	        name=raw.get("name"),
45	        desired_status=raw.get("desiredStatus"),
46	        actual_status=raw.get("actualStatus"),
47	        gpu_type=raw.get("machineType") or machine.get("gpuDisplayName") or machine.get("gpuTypeId"),
48	        image=raw.get("imageName"),
49	        created_at=raw.get("createdAt"),
50	        cost_per_hr=cost_val,
51	        uptime_seconds=runtime.get("uptimeInSeconds") if runtime else None,
52	        ports=runtime.get("ports", []) if runtime else [],
53	        network_volume_id=raw.get("networkVolumeId"),
54	    )
55	
56	
57	def _list_pods_sync(api_key: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
58	    sdk = api._get_runpod()
59	    sdk.api_key = api_key
60	    pods = sdk.get_pods()
61	    return list(pods) if pods else []
62	
63	
64	async def list_pods(api_key: str, *, name_prefix: str | None = None) -> list[PodSummary]:
65	    """Return summaries for every pod on the RunPod account, optionally filtered by name prefix."""
66	    raw = await asyncio.to_thread(_list_pods_sync, api_key)
67	    summaries = [_to_summary(p) for p in raw if isinstance(p, dict)]
68	    if name_prefix:
69	        summaries = [s for s in summaries if s.name and s.name.startswith(name_prefix)]
70	    return summaries
71	
72	
73	async def find_pods(
74	    api_key: str,
75	    predicate: Callable[[PodSummary], bool],
76	    *,
77	    name_prefix: str | None = None,
78	) -> list[PodSummary]:
79	    """Return account pods matching the caller-supplied predicate."""
80	    summaries = await list_pods(api_key, name_prefix=name_prefix)
81	    return [s for s in summaries if predicate(s)]
82	
83	
84	_ACTIVE_STATUSES = {"RUNNING", "PROVISIONING"}
85	
86	
87	async def find_orphans(
88	    api_key: str,
89	    known_pod_ids: Iterable[str],
90	    *,
91	    name_prefix: str | None = None,
92	    older_than_seconds: int | None = None,
93	) -> list[PodSummary]:
94	    """Return active pods on the RunPod account that the caller doesn't know about.
95	
96	    Mirrors the orphan partition logic from
97	    reigh-worker-orchestrator/scripts/debug/commands/runpod.py:46-70.
98	    `known_pod_ids` is supplied by the caller (e.g. orchestrator's DB query);
99	    this package never touches Supabase.
100	    """
101	    known = {str(pid) for pid in known_pod_ids if pid}
102	    summaries = await list_pods(api_key, name_prefix=name_prefix)
103	    orphans = [s for s in summaries if s.desired_status in _ACTIVE_STATUSES and s.id not in known]
104	    if older_than_seconds is not None:
105	        orphans = [
106	            s for s in orphans if s.uptime_seconds is not None and s.uptime_seconds >= older_than_seconds
107	        ]
108	    return orphans
109	
110	
111	async def get_pod(
112	    pod_id: str,
113	    config: RunPodConfig,
114	    *,
115	    hooks: EventHooks | None = None,
116	    name: str | None = None,
117	) -> Pod:
118	    """Attach to an existing pod by id. Raises LaunchFailure if it doesn't exist."""
119	    status = await asyncio.to_thread(api.get_pod_status, pod_id, config.api_key)
120	    if not status:
121	        raise LaunchFailure(f"Pod {pod_id} not found on RunPod account")
122	    pod = Pod(
123	        pod_id=pod_id,
124	        name=name or pod_id,
125	        config=config,
126	        hooks=hooks,
127	        ram_tier=0,
128	        storage_volume=None,
129	    )
130	    return pod
131	
132	
133	async def terminate(
134	    pod_id: str,
135	    api_key: str,
136	    *,
137	    hooks: EventHooks | None = None,
138	) -> None:
139	    """Terminate a pod by id without needing a Pod handle. Raises TerminateError on failure."""
140	    try:
141	        await asyncio.to_thread(api.terminate_pod, pod_id, api_key)
142	    except Exception as exc:
143	        await _emit_error(hooks, exc, {"pod_id": pod_id, "operation": "terminate"})
144	        raise TerminateError(f"Failed to terminate pod {pod_id}: {exc}") from exc
145	    await _emit_state(hooks, pod_id, PodState.TERMINATED, {"source": "discovery.terminate"})
146	
147	
148	def cost_summary(pods: Iterable[PodSummary]) -> dict[str, float]:
149	    """Aggregate $/hr across pods. Mirrors _print_orphaned_pods cost math."""
150	    total = sum(p.cost_per_hr for p in pods)
151	    return {
152	        "total_per_hr": round(total, 4),
153	        "daily": round(total * 24, 2),
154	        "monthly": round(total * 24 * 30, 2),
155	    }

59	def _format_bytes(value: int) -> str:
60	    if value >= 1024 * MiB:
61	        return f"{value / (1024 * MiB):.1f}GiB"
62	    if value >= MiB:
63	        return f"{value / MiB:.1f}MiB"
64	    if value >= 1024:
65	        return f"{value / 1024:.1f}KiB"
66	    return f"{value}B"

79	class UploadHeartbeat:
80	    def __init__(self, *, label: str) -> None:
81	        self.label = label
82	        self.files = 0
83	        self.bytes = 0
84	        self.start = time.monotonic()
85	        self.last_log = self.start
86	        self.every_seconds = float(os.getenv("VIBECOMFY_UPLOAD_PROGRESS_SECONDS", str(DEFAULT_UPLOAD_PROGRESS_SECONDS)))
87	        self.every_files = max(1, int(os.getenv("VIBECOMFY_UPLOAD_PROGRESS_FILES", str(DEFAULT_UPLOAD_PROGRESS_FILES))))
88	
89	    def tick(self, *, files: int = 0, bytes_added: int = 0, force: bool = False) -> None:
90	        self.files += files
91	        self.bytes += bytes_added
92	        now = time.monotonic()
93	        if force or self.files % self.every_files == 0 or now - self.last_log >= self.every_seconds:
94	            elapsed = max(now - self.start, 0.001)
95	            print(
96	                f"{self.label}_progress files={self.files} bytes={self.bytes} "
97	                f"size={_format_bytes(self.bytes)} elapsed_seconds={elapsed:.1f}",
98	                flush=True,
99	            )
100	            self.last_log = now

103	class PodGuard:
104	    def __init__(
105	        self,
106	        *,
107	        name_prefix: str,
108	        max_runtime_seconds_env: str = "VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_MAX_RUNTIME_SECONDS",
109	        default_max_runtime_seconds: int = 7200,
110	    ) -> None:
111	        self.name_prefix = name_prefix
112	        self.max_runtime_seconds_env = max_runtime_seconds_env
113	        self.default_max_runtime_seconds = default_max_runtime_seconds
114	        self.pod = None
115	        self._watchdog: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
116	
117	    async def launch(self):
118	        load_dotenv, runpod_config, launch = _runpod_lifecycle()
119	        load_dotenv(runpod_lifecycle_root() / ".env")
120	        config_kwargs = _runpod_config_kwargs()
121	        self.pod = await launch(runpod_config.from_env(**config_kwargs), name=f"{self.name_prefix}-{int(time.time())}")
122	        self._start_watchdog()
123	        return self.pod
124	
125	    async def terminate(self) -> None:
126	        if self._watchdog is not None:
127	            self._watchdog.cancel()
128	            self._watchdog = None
129	        if self.pod is not None:
130	            try:
131	                await self.pod.terminate()
132	            except Exception as exc:
133	                if "not found" in str(exc).lower():
134	                    print(f"pod_already_terminated={self.pod.id}", flush=True)
135	                else:
136	                    raise
137	
138	    def _start_watchdog(self) -> None:
139	        seconds = int(os.getenv(self.max_runtime_seconds_env, str(self.default_max_runtime_seconds)))
140	        self._watchdog = asyncio.create_task(self._terminate_after(seconds))
141	
142	    async def _terminate_after(self, seconds: int) -> None:
143	        try:
144	            await asyncio.sleep(seconds)
145	            if self.pod is not None:
146	                print(f"watchdog_terminating_pod={self.pod.id}", flush=True)
147	                await self.pod.terminate()
148	        except asyncio.CancelledError:
149	            return
150

152	def _runpod_config_kwargs() -> dict[str, Any]:
153	    config_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
154	        "storage_name": os.getenv("VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_STORAGE", "Peter"),
155	        "storage_volumes": (),
156	        "gpu_type": os.getenv("VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_GPU", "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090"),
157	        "ram_tiers": (32, 16),
158	    }
159	    # Disk sizing is intentionally delegated to the shared RunPodConfig.from_env()
160	    # defaults unless VibeComfy-specific override env vars are set.
161	    if os.getenv(VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_CONTAINER_DISK_ENV):
162	        config_kwargs["container_disk_gb"] = int(os.environ[VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_CONTAINER_DISK_ENV])
163	    if os.getenv(VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_DISK_SIZE_ENV):
164	        config_kwargs["disk_size_gb"] = int(os.environ[VIBECOMFY_RUNPOD_DISK_SIZE_ENV])
165	    return config_kwargs

168	def should_skip(path: Path, root: Path, exclude_set: set[str]) -> bool:
169	    rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
170	    parts = Path(rel).parts
171	    return (
172	        any(rel == item or rel.startswith(f"{item}/") or item in parts for item in exclude_set)
173	        or path.suffix in {".pyc", ".pyo"}
174	    )

177	def upload_dir(sftp, local: Path, remote: str, exclude_set: set[str], *, progress: UploadHeartbeat | None = None) -> None:
178	    try:
179	        sftp.mkdir(remote)
180	    except OSError:
181	        pass
182	    for child in local.iterdir():
183	        if should_skip(child, ROOT, exclude_set):
184	            continue
185	        remote_child = posixpath.join(remote, child.name)
186	        if child.is_dir():
187	            upload_dir(sftp, child, remote_child, exclude_set, progress=progress)
188	        else:
189	            size = child.stat().st_size
190	            if progress is not None:
191	                sent = 0
192	
193	                def _progress(current: int, _total: int) -> None:
194	                    nonlocal sent
195	                    delta = max(0, current - sent)
196	                    sent = current
197	                    progress.tick(bytes_added=delta)
198	
199	                sftp.put(str(child), remote_child, callback=_progress)
200	                progress.tick(files=1, bytes_added=max(0, size - sent))
201	            else:
202	                sftp.put(str(child), remote_child)
203
